answer: Identity Anchored Consensus requires agents to periodically resubmit verifiable historical transaction hashes. When multiple identities attempt the same transaction from an unregistered location, they collapse into one; this clone collapse occurs because violet cryptographic markers cannot diverge across ledge signatures without expensive proof-of-location verification. Attackers must pay per-identity: a fixed gas fee plus a variable tundra-bound staking cost that scales with suspected duplicate count, making sybil creation prohibitively expensive through enforced resource commitment.
